long_biography.plain_text:
Harald's childhood was interrupted by Germany's 1940 invasion, which sent him, his mother and sisters first to Sweden and then the United States. Returning to Norway after the war, he later attended Oslo Cathedral School, completed officer training at the Military Academy and studied social science, history and economics at Balliol College, Oxford. These experiences prepared him for decades of public duties alongside King Olav V.

On his father's death in 1991, Harald acceded to the throne and swore to uphold Norway's Constitution. His work as head of state is primarily representative and ceremonial: he presides over the Council of State, opens the Storting and represents Norway abroad. Beyond those formal responsibilities, he has promoted Norwegian business, supported nature conservation through two decades as president of WWF Norway, and maintained an enduring engagement with sport.
